doc_description: Johnson & Johnson’s Q2 2023 earnings release: 6.3% reported sales growth (8.9% ex–COVID-19 vaccine), strong MedTech momentum including Abiomed, detailed regional/segment results and notable regulatory updates, raised full‑year 2023 guidance, a planned Kenvue split‑off, and extensive non‑GAAP reconciliations with webcast information.

structure.title: OVERALL FINANCIAL RESULTS
structure.heading: 1 OVERALL FINANCIAL RESULTS
structure.start_phrase: 1 Non-GAAP financial measure ; refer to reconciliations of non -GAAP financial measures included in accompanying schedules
structure.summary:
- Johnson & Johnson reported Q2 2023 results showing strong growth and raised full-year guidance.
- Reported sales grew 6.3% to $25.5 billion; operational sales up 7.5% and adjusted operational sales up 6.2%. Operational growth excluding COVID-19 vaccine was 8.9%.
- Diluted EPS was $1.96, up 8.9%; adjusted diluted EPS was $2.80, up 8.1%.
- Net earnings were $5.144 billion (up 6.9%); adjusted net earnings were $7.358 billion (up 6.5%).
- The company is increasing 2023 full-year guidance midpoints for adjusted operational sales excluding COVID-19 vaccine and for adjusted operational EPS.
- Johnson & Johnson intends to “split off” Kenvue shares via an exchange offer as the next step in its separation, subject to market conditions.
- CEO Joaquin Duato highlighted robust first-half performance and the company’s transition to a two-sector focus on Pharmaceutical and MedTech innovation.
- Non-GAAP notes: metrics exclude impacts such as translational currency, acquisitions/divestitures, intangible amortization, and special items; values may be rounded.

structure.title: REGIONAL SALES RESULTS
structure.heading: 2 REGIONAL SALES RESULTS
structure.start_phrase: 1 Non-GAAP financial measure ; refer to reconciliations of non -GAAP financial measures included in accompanying schedules
structure.summary:
The document presents Q2 2023 sales results versus Q2 2022, detailing performance by region and business segment, with growth shown on a reported, operational (non-GAAP), currency impact, and adjusted operational (excluding acquisitions/divestitures and currency) basis. Key points:
- Worldwide sales: $25,530M vs $24,020M, up 6.3% reported; 7.5% operational; currency drag of 1.2 pts; adjusted operational growth 6.2%.
- Regional:
  - U.S.: $13,444M vs $12,197M, up 10.2% reported and operational; no currency impact; adjusted operational growth 8.0%.
  - International: $12,086M vs $11,823M, up 2.2% reported; 4.7% operational; currency impact −2.5 pts; adjusted operational 4.4%.
- Segments:
  - Consumer Health: $4,011M vs $3,805M, up 5.4% reported; 7.7% operational; currency −2.3 pts; adjusted operational 7.7%.
  - Pharmaceutical: $13,731M vs $13,317M, up 3.1% reported; 3.8% operational; currency −0.7 pts; adjusted operational 3.9%.
  - MedTech: $7,788M vs $6,898M, up 12.9% reported; 14.7% operational; currency −1.8 pts; adjusted operational 9.9%.
Additional notes: Operational and adjusted operational are non-GAAP measures; operational excludes translational currency; adjusted operational excludes both currency and net impacts of acquisitions/divestitures; values may be rounded.

structure.title: SECOND QUARTER 2023 SEGMENT COMMENTARY
structure.heading: 4 SECOND QUARTER 2023 SEGMENT COMMENTARY
structure.start_phrase: Adjusted operational sales* reflected below exclude s the net impact of acquisitions and divestitures and translational currency.
structure.summary:
- Overview: Q2 2023 segment commentary focusing on adjusted operational sales (excluding acquisitions/divestitures and currency) across Pharmaceutical, MedTech, and Consumer Health, plus references to regulatory filings and investor information.
- Pharmaceutical: Adjusted operational sales up 3.9%; up 6.2% excluding the COVID-19 vaccine. Growth driven by DARZALEX, ERLEADA, CARVYKTI (Oncology), STELARA and TREMFYA (Immunology), UPTRAVI and OPSUMIT (Pulmonary Hypertension), and SPRAVATO (Neuroscience). Partially offset by declines in ZYTIGA and IMBRUVICA (Oncology), the COVID-19 vaccine (Infectious Diseases), and REMICADE (Immunology).
- MedTech: Adjusted operational sales up 9.9%, led by electrophysiology (Interventional Solutions), trauma (Orthopaedics), wound closure (General Surgery), biosurgery (Advanced Surgery), and contact lenses (Vision). Total operational sales up 14.7%, with the Abiomed acquisition contributing 4.8%.
- Consumer Health: Adjusted operational sales up 7.7%, largely from OTC products—TYLENOL and MOTRIN analgesics, upper respiratory, international smoking cessation, and IMODIUM—plus NEUTROGENA (Skin Health/Beauty) and Women’s Health products outside the U.S.
- Notable announcements: Directs readers to review SEC filings and company investor resources, including dedicated information sites on talc, prescription opioids, and LTL Management.

- MedTech: Adjusted operational sales grew 9.9%, driven by electrophysiology (Interventional Solutions), trauma (Orthopaedics), wound closure (General Surgery), biosurgery (Advanced Surgery), and contact lenses (Vision). Total operational sales grew 14.7%, with the Abiomed acquisition contributing 4.8%.
- Consumer Health: Adjusted operational sales increased 7.7%, largely from OTC products—TYLENOL and MOTRIN analgesics, upper respiratory, international smoking cessation, and IMODIUM—plus growth in NEUTROGENA (Skin Health/Beauty) and Women’s Health products outside the U.S.
- Notable announcements: References to SEC filings (Forms 8-K, 10-Q, 10-K) and company investor resources, including dedicated information sites on talc, prescription opioids, and LTL Management.

structure.heading: 5 NOTABLE NEW ANNOUNCEMENTS IN THE QUARTER
structure.start_phrase: The information contained in this section should be read in conjunction with Johnson & Johnson’s other disclosures filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including its Current Reports on Form 8 -K, Quarterly Reports on Form 10 -Q and Annual Repor ts on Form 10 -K.
structure.summary:
- Overview: Johnson & Johnson’s Q2 2023 segment commentary, with adjusted operational sales excluding acquisitions/divestitures and currency, plus notable regulatory, clinical, and corporate announcements.
- Pharmaceutical: Adjusted operational sales up 3.9% (6.2% excluding COVID-19 vaccine). Growth driven by DARZALEX, ERLEADA, CARVYKTI (Oncology); STELARA, TREMFYA (Immunology); UPTRAVI, OPSUMIT (Pulmonary Hypertension); and SPRAVATO (Neuroscience). Partly offset by declines in ZYTIGA, IMBRUVICA (Oncology), COVID-19 vaccine (Ad26.COV2.S), and REMICADE (Immunology).
- MedTech: Adjusted operational sales up 9.9%, led by electrophysiology (Interventional Solutions), trauma (Orthopaedics), wound closure (General Surgery), biosurgery (Advanced Surgery), and contact lenses (Vision). Total operational sales up 14.7%, with 4.8% contribution from the Abiomed acquisition.
- Consumer Health: Adjusted operational sales up 7.7%, mainly from OTC products (TYLENOL, MOTRIN, upper respiratory remedies, international smoking cessation, IMODIUM), plus NEUTROGENA (Skin Health/Beauty) and Women’s Health outside the U.S.
- Notable announcements (regulatory/clinical):
  - EC authorization for AKEEGA (niraparib + abiraterone) in BRCA1/2-mutated mCRPC.
  - FDA Fast Track for milvexian across ischemic stroke, ACS, and AFib (Librexia Phase 3).
  - NDA to FDA for macitentan + tadalafil single-tablet combo in PAH.
  - sBLA to FDA for earlier-line use of CARVYKTI in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma.
  - Positive data across programs: TAR-200 + cetrelimab in BCG-unresponsive NMIBC (Phase 2); first Phase 3 TREMFYA UC induction results; QDOT MICRO catheter data in AFib; over 90 oncology presentations at ASCO/EHA; Phase 2 nipocalimab in high-risk HDFN; positive topline for oral IL-23 peptide JNJ-2113 in psoriasis; RYBREVANT + chemo improved PFS in EGFR Exon 20 insertion NSCLC (some noted as post-quarter).
- Other corporate items: Launch of Kenvue Inc. IPO roadshow; collaboration and license agreement with Cellular Biomedicine Group for next-generation CAR-T therapies.
- Reference to SEC filings and investor resources for additional details and disclosures.

  - Vision (Contact Lenses/Other, Surgical): Mid-single-digit worldwide growth; Contact Lenses/Other strong in the U.S.; Surgical up internationally but flat-to-down in the U.S.

- Pharmaceutical segment coverage and trends:
  - U.S. grows high single digits; International down on a reported basis with FX pressure but better on an operational basis.
  - Worldwide pharma Q2 up 3.1% reported (+3.8% operational); first half up 3.7% reported (+5.5% operational).

    - Q2 worldwide sales increased to 13,731 from 13,317 (+3.1% total; +3.8% operational; -0.7% currency). U.S. grew 9.2%; International declined 4.0% (impacted by currency).
    - YTD worldwide sales rose to 27,144 from 26,186 (+3.7% total; +5.5% operational; -1.8% currency).
  - COVID-19 Vaccine (separately disclosed):
    - Q2 worldwide sales fell to 285 from 544 (-47.7% total; -51.8% operational; +4.1% currency). U.S. had no sales vs 45 prior year; International declined 43%.
    - YTD worldwide sales were 1,032 vs 1,001 (+3.0% total; +4.2% operational; -1.2% currency).
  - Pharmaceutical excluding COVID-19 Vaccine:
    - Q2 worldwide sales increased to 13,446 from 12,773 (+5.3% total; +6.2% operational; -0.9% currency). U.S. grew 9.9%; International was roughly flat on a reported basis (slight decline due to currency) but up operationally.
    - YTD worldwide sales were 26,112 vs 25,185 (+3.7% total; +5.5% operational; -1.8% currency).
- Total company sales:
  - Q2 worldwide totaled 25,530 vs 24,020 (+6.3% total; +7.5% operational; -1.2% currency). U.S. grew 10.2%; International grew 2.2% (4.7% operational, -2.5% currency).
  - Excluding COVID-19 Vaccine, Q2 worldwide sales were 25,245 vs 23,476 (+7.5% total; +8.9% operational; -1.4% currency).
  - YTD worldwide totaled 50,276 vs 47,446 (+6.0% total; +8.2% operational; -2.2% currency). Excluding COVID-19 Vaccine, YTD worldwide sales were 49,244 vs 46,445 (+6.0% total; +8.3% operational; -2.3% currency).
- Non-GAAP reconciliation (Income Before Tax by segment):
  - Reported Income Before Tax (2023 vs 2022): Consumer Health 860 vs 784; Pharmaceutical 4,862 vs 4,420; MedTech 1,699 vs 1,141; Unallocated (377) vs (237); Consumer Health separation costs (282) vs (268); Worldwide Total 6,762 vs 5,840. Reported margin: 26.5% vs 24.3% of sales.
  - Adjustments include: intangible asset amortization, litigation-related items, COVID-19 vaccine-related costs, gains/losses on securities, restructuring-related items, acquisition/integration/divestiture costs, Medical Device Regulation costs, and Consumer Health separation costs.
  - Adjusted Income Before Tax (2023 vs 2022): Consumer Health 941 vs 987; Pharmaceutical 5,865 vs 5,593; MedTech 2,225 vs 1,828; Unallocated (207) vs (237); separation costs removed; Worldwide Total 8,824 vs 8,171. Adjusted margin: 34.6% vs 34.0% of sales.
- Additional notes:
  - Columns/rows may not add due to rounding; asterisk indicates percentages greater than 100% or not meaningful.
  - Some figures noted as estimated as of 7/20/2023.

- Adjustments detailed: Intangible asset amortization, in-process R&D, litigation-related items, COVID-19 vaccine–related costs, gains/losses on securities, restructuring, acquisition/integration/divestiture costs, Medical Device Regulation (MDR) costs, Consumer Health separation costs, and other items.

  - Worldwide adjusted income before tax rose to 8,824 from 8,171; adjusted margin 34.6% vs 34.0%.

structure.title: Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures
structure.heading: 15 Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures
structure.summary:
- Purpose: Reconciles Johnson & Johnson’s GAAP results to Non-GAAP measures.
- Scope and timing: Second quarter and year-to-date (six months) ended July 2, 2023 versus July 3, 2022; amounts in millions; includes an estimate note dated 7/20/2023.
- Segmentation: Presents Income Before Tax by segment—Consumer Health, Pharmaceutical, MedTech, Unallocated—and a Worldwide Total, with each shown as dollars and percent to sales for both reported (GAAP) and adjusted (Non-GAAP).
- Key adjustments to derive Non-GAAP: 
  - Intangible asset amortization
  - In-process research and development (IPR&D)
  - Litigation-related items
  - COVID-19 vaccine–related costs
  - Loss/(gain) on securities
  - Restructuring-related items
  - Acquisition, integration and divestiture–related items
  - Medical Device Regulation (MDR) costs
  - Consumer Health separation costs
  - Other adjustments
  - Related tax effects, including tax legislation impacts and Consumer Health separation tax-related costs
- Consolidated GAAP-to-Non-GAAP bridges: Line-item reconciliations for cost of products sold, selling/marketing/admin, research and development, other (income)/expense, interest, restructuring, provision for taxes, and net earnings for Q2 and year-to-date in both 2023 and 2022.
- Highlights reflected in the tables: 
  - Adjusted Income Before Tax and margin by segment and in total, showing improvements versus reported figures.
  - Identification of large non-operational items (e.g., litigation, securities gains/losses, separation and MDR costs) concentrated in Other (Income)/Expense and Unallocated.
- Overall: Provides transparency on how one-time or non-core items affect reported results and the resulting adjusted metrics management uses to assess underlying performance.
